prompt: Build a modern luxury villa on the coast: cantilevered white concrete volumes, floor-to-ceiling glass, an infinity pool, a rooftop terrace with plants, and a minimalist interior.
detail: I built the modern villa on the riverbank. The job used about $1.40 of the $6 budget. - **Cantilevered volumes:** the white concrete bedroo…

finished.summary: I built a two-level modern villa on the riverbank. A white concrete bedroom wing sits crosswise on top of a glass-walled living pavilion and cantilevers 10 blocks out toward the water. A long infinity pool with a glass end wall sticks out over the river bank, and above it all are planted roof terraces and a lounge pavilion.
highlights: Upper bedroom wing cantilevered 10 blocks west and 4 blocks south with no supports underneath
Infinity pool: a glass end wall over the river, lights set into the pool floor, one slender column
Floor-to-ceiling glass between quartz fins on the ground floor and the upper wing
Rooftop with a spruce deck, azalea/bamboo planters, sunbeds and a shaded lounge pavilion
Lower roof terrace with a fire pit, a plunge pool and floating quartz stairs
Minimalist interior: white L-shaped sofa, pale-oak dining table, black kitchen island, oak headboard wall; all lighting hidden in ceilings and floors
suggestions: Build op errors abort the whole batch on one bad op (e.g. an unknown mask). An option like `skipInvalid:true` that runs the valid ops and reports the bad ones would save a costly resend of 40+ ops.

The render shows glass and glass panes as nearly invisible, so glazed facades look like open frames and glass railings can't be checked. A slight tint/reflection or an edge outline for glass would help review.

The 'front' render view slices through the river at the edge of the box, so it looks like a cross-section. An option to render the elevation from outside the terrain cut (no section fill) would make facade review clearer.
A `slab_edge`/`fascia` op for modern builds (projecting rim around a floor plate, with an optional light strip) would speed up cantilever detailing.
terraform flatten with blend left a hard polished/dirt edge where the pad meets the riverbank; a `retaining_wall` option (material + follows the pad edge down to the ground) would be useful.
